Introduction
We are upgrading a section of the Waterloop Trail to
better serve pedestrians, cyclists and other active modes of transportation by
making a key connection in the City’s off-road trail network. Follow this page for ongoing project updates on design and construction.
The Waterloop pathway system was identified through Waterloo's Transportation Master
Plan for upgrades because of its proximity to the
community center; library; schools; and links to existing area multi-use-paths
and on-road bike lanes plus connections to ION stations.
The main project areas are:
Upgrade the stone dust trail with asphalt to enhance accessibility and improved drainage.
Increase the trail width to 3 metres to accommodate all modes of active transportation.
Provide pedestrian scale lighting for a safer environment outside of daylight hours.
Remove barriers affecting accessibility.
Provide a trail link that will be maintained and available all year round.
The project has two parts. Part one is upgrading a section of the existing trail. Part two is removing some existing trail and bridges and realigning a portion of the trail.
This includes:
Replacing approximately 230m of stone dust trail with asphalt between Parkside Drive and Old Albert Street (behind the Albert McCormick Community Center).
Removing approximately 200m of stone dust trail and 2 pedestrian bridges.
Creating a new asphalt trail alignment north of 525 Albert Street.
Converting approximately 75m of sidewalk to a multi-use-path along Albert Street to connect active users to the existing pedestrian island.

FAQ
Why was the trail in Old Albert Park realigned?
A 2024 structural assessment of City pedestrian bridges identified major repairs were needed to the Pedestrian Bridge (PB#15) which crosses over Cedar Creek.
PB#15 did not comply with current legislation, is only 2 metres wide so does not support increased active use and presented a barrier for persons with disabilities.
The City completed an assessment on replacing the bridge but the cost was significant. Additionally, the construction would impact the surrounding environment.
Reconstructing the existing trail created drainage challenges that could have potentially caused flooding problems.
A 2024 structural assessment noted Pedestrian Bridge PB#108 was in good condition and will be removed and repurposed.
How will the new trail alignment connect to existing trail?
A section of sidewalk on Albert Street will be replaced with
a new asphalt multi-use-path (MUP) between the trail head and the pedestrian
island north of the park. This MUP will permit cyclists to legally travel north
to cross Albert Street at the island to continue their journey towards Weber
Street. The existing cycle track only permits cyclists to travel southbound.
Will the new trail alignment impact the adjacent property at 525 Albert Street.
The new trail alignment will be located within municipally
owned lands.
What impact will the construction of the new trail have on the forested area?
The City of Waterloo’s arborist has reviewed the area and
has determined there is no significant species impacted in the forested
area proposed for the new trail alignment. The area to be cleared for
construction will be managed carefully to ensure minimal impact to the area.
All areas affected by construction will be restored to existing conditions
or better. A planting plan will be prepared as part of the detailed design and
include native trees to be planted in the area.
This project is being planned and designed in consultation with the
Grand River Conservation Area (GRCA).
Will the trail be maintained in winter?
Yes, as it is part of the City's primary network.
